title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Canary failed in prod-ish cluster (canary lane) after a config-only deploy + image bump. Goal: map artifact -> deployment -> root cause and get safe rollback path.

Timeline / key events (observed):
- 2026-03-04 02:16 UTC: pipeline #987654 finished successfully (build + helm chart release). Image tag: service:2026-03-04-rc3 (digest sha256:abcd1234...).
- 2026-03-04 02:22 UTC: Canary rollout started (1 pod canary, 10% traffic).
- 2026-03-04 ~02:28 UTC: Health check 502s from canary; latency spikes; error rate up.
- 02:31 UTC: Autoscaler did not trigger because replica target = 1 for canary stage.
- 02:34 UTC: Canary marked unhealthy by rollout controller; automatic pause triggered.
- 02:40 UTC: Manual intervention: rollback requested.

Notes-to-self / commands tried (raw outputs trimmed):
- Check pipeline and image mapping:
  curl -s "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/redwood-inference%2Fplatform/pipelines/987654" | jq '.status,.sha'
  # confirmed pipeline status: "success", sha: "f1e2d3c4"

- Image digest verification (local):
  gcloud container images list-tags gcr.io/redwood-inference/service --filter="tags:2026-03-04-rc3" --limit=1 --format='get(digest)'
  -> returned: sha256:abcd1234 (matches pipeline metadata).

- Deployment status & events (kube canary namespace):
  kubectl -n canary get deploy/service-canary -o yaml | egrep "image:|replicas:|strategy:" -n
  kubectl -n canary describe rs -l app=service -n canary
  # Events: FailedCreatePod -> CrashLoopBackOff? No. Image pulled ok.
  # Events show: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 502" on new pod(s).

- Pod logs (canary pod):
  kubectl -n canary logs service-canary-abcde -c main --since=30m
  -> repeated stack traces: upstream service returned 502, and internal 5xx due to a specific upstream timeout to feature-store (timeout=1s).

- Grep for config changes in helm values: (we changed only two keys per release notes)
  git --no-pager show f1e2d3c4:charts/service/values.yaml | sed -n '1,200p' | egrep "feature_store|timeout|connection"
  -> found: featureStore.timeoutMs: 1000 (previous releases used 3000).
  -> aha. PR #1234 bumped timeout down to improve tail latency.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Config regression: featureStore.timeoutMs reduced from 3000 -> 1000 ms. Under production load, some upstream calls exceed 1s and return 502, causing readiness failures and canary failure. (strong)
2) Artifact mismatch: chart rendered references wrong configmap key due to templating bug causing default 1000 to be applied even when values had 3000. (possible)
3) Upstream transient incident coincidentally during canary window. (weak)
4) Image bug: new image has changed retry semantics which combined with lower timeout caused cascading failures. (medium)

Commands to confirm hypotheses / next steps tried: 
- Inspect rendered helm manifest used by CI: CI stores rendered manifests at artifacts/helm-render/service-987654.yaml
  # pulled artifact and searched for timeout value
  grep -n "timeoutMs" artifacts/helm-render/service-987654.yaml || true
  -> shows featureStore.timeoutMs: 1000 in rendered manifest => templating produced 1000.

- Check values used by release job (pipeline YAML variables):
  curl -s "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/.../variables" | jq '.[] | select(.key=="RELEASE_VALUES_SHA")'
  -> RELEASE_VALUES_SHA points to f1e2d3c4-values.yaml (yep). Downloaded and confirmed it has 1000.

- Compare previous release (rc2) values:
  gcloud storage cp gs://redwood-deploy-values/service/2026-03-03-rc2/values.yaml - | egrep "featureStore.timeoutMs" -n || true
  -> previous release shows 3000.

- Quick sanity: curl /.health endpoints on canary pod locally (port-forward) to reproduce 502:
  kubectl -n canary port-forward pod/service-canary-abcde 8080:8080 &
  curl -v http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
  -> 502, with log snippet: "feature-store timeout after 1000ms, upstream returned 502"

Decision and rollback plan notes:
- Root cause most likely config change in values.yaml (intentional PR change to reduce tail latencies). Rolling back to previous values (3000) should restore stability for canary.
- Options:
  A) Quick patch: patch configmap / deployment to bump featureStore.timeoutMs -> 3000 and restart canary pod. (fastest)
  B) Full rollback: trigger ingress of previous chart release (rc2) via helm rollback or re-deploy image:service:2026-03-03-rc2 + rc2 values. (safer if image change suspected)
  C) Bake a hotfix: revert PR #1234 in values repo and rerun pipeline. (clean but slower)

Commands used to patch (tested in staging first):
- kubectl -n canary set env deployment/service-canary FEATURE_STORE_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
  # Note: we currently prefer values file over env var; but service also reads env fallback.

- Helm rollback command (tested in dry-run):
  helm -n canary rollback service 2 --wait --timeout 5m --dry-run
  -> dry-run looked OK (reverted values to rc2 set).

Manual rollback executed (what actually happened):
- Took path A + B: patched env for immediate mitigation and then rolled back helm release to rc2 image + values.
- Commands executed (ops runbook):
  kubectl -n canary set env deployment/service-canary FEATURE_STORE_TIMEOUT_MS=3000
  helm -n canary rollback service 2 --wait

Observed after rollback:
- Within ~45s readiness started passing, ReplicaSet stabilized to desired replicas=1, canary traffic resumed, error rate dropped to baseline.
- No image pull errors; image digest for rc2 confirmed: sha256:ffff1111.

Postmortem notes / TODOs (for later):
- Add a guarding check in CI: compare values.yaml changes for critical timeouts and require +2 approvals for changes to featureStore.* and retry.* settings. (prevent single-PR regressions)
- Improve canary policy: make canary scale to >=2 replicas to avoid single-pod single-point-of-failure/false-positive.
- Chart templating test: add unit test in chart-ci to render values with both new and default vars and assert that timeout values match expected keys.
- Observability: link the pipeline id and image digest into the rollout events so oncall can quickly map pipeline->manifest->helm release (we have artifacts but not surfaced in rollout UI).
- On-call playbook: explicit runbook: if readiness fails with 5xx referencing feature-store timeouts, first check values for featureStore.timeoutMs before rolling back image.

Notes / open questions:
- Why was the intentional change made (PR #1234) — author notes claimed tail-latency reduction in dev. Need to find perf test that justified 1000ms.
- Is there any change to retries in the new image that reduces upstream resilience? Need to compare network/retry code between rc2 and rc3.

References / links (artifacts/trace):
- Pipeline: gitlab.com/redwood-inference/platform/-/pipelines/987654
- Helm rendered manifest artifact: artifacts/helm-render/service-987654.yaml
- PR: gitlab.com/redwood-inference/platform/-/merge_requests/1234
- Incident channel: slack workspace: #incidents (thread ts: 1678000000.000100)

Short checklist for writing final incident note:
- Summary: config change (timeout) in release rc3 caused canary to fail -> rolled back to rc2 values+image -> stability restored.
- Impact: brief canary pause, no full-prod rollout; no customer-facing downtime (caught by canary).
- Root cause: values.yaml change (featureStore.timeoutMs 3000 -> 1000) + insufficient guardrails and single-pod canary.
- Actions: revert/patch, chart CI tests, approval policy, canary scaling change, update runbook.

Random breadcrumbs for traceability (copy-pasteable):
- kubectl -n canary describe deploy service-canary | egrep -A3 "Events|Conditions"
- kubectl -n canary logs service-canary-abcde -c main --since=1h | egrep "timeout|feature-store|502" -n
- gsutil cp gs://redwood-deploy-values/service/2026-03-03-rc2/values.yaml - | sed -n '1,200p' | egrep "featureStore|timeout"

End of scratchpad. Will convert this into a short incident summary and follow-up ticket (JIRA-RELEASE-2143) after verifying whether new image changed retry semantics.

Notes-to-self: keep this file as personal breadcrumbs (timestamped). Move to shared docs/incidents once postmortem draft is ready.
